origin: The kernel: smuggling cases exist, China's best models trail the US frontier by months, Chinese labs report far less compute, and the (unverified) Liang transcript itself names insufficient production capacity as the only problem for domestic chips. The contestable parts: "rampant" smuggling rests on individual cases; "limited domestic production capacity" is asserted without a figure, and the transcript's remark is a statement, not a quantity; and "cannot build more powerful models than the US without US chips" is a causal inference presented as settled. Expected honest rating: 60 to 75 (raised from the drafter's 55 to 70 by this consolidation, because the added Liang line supports the post's premise; not re-estimated by the verifier).
author: Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic

evidence_up.evidence_note: Real. Epoch AI, Venkat Somala, "Will Huawei catch up to Nvidia by 2030?", https://epoch.ai/publications/huaweis-roadmap-to-2031, announced on X on 4 September 2026, 19:45:00 UTC (https://x.com/EpochAIResearch/status/2095961343648211412), after the 27 July post. Published 2026-09-04. Verbatim: "Its most powerful chip, the Ascend 950, delivers roughly half the performance of Nvidia's H100, which began shipping in 2022, and Huawei will produce less than 4% of Nvidia's compute output this year." "In the near term, limited supply of high-bandwidth memory (HBM) is the binding constraint on Huawei's production. Even after supplementing domestic HBM with stockpiles of foreign HBM, lower-bandwidth memory alternatives, and smuggled HBM, we estimate Huawei will produce less than 4% as much AI compute as Nvidia in 2026. Using only Chinese-made HBM, its output could remain around 1% of Nvidia's through 2028." "Even if Huawei smuggled 10× as much usable HBM as its entire domestic supply in 2028, its output would still be only about 16% of Nvidia's."
pushes: New information that adds to the fact sheet: on September 4, 2026, Epoch AI published an analysis of Huawei's AI chip roadmap and supply chain. It estimates that Huawei will produce less than 4% as much AI compute as Nvidia in 2026, and that its most powerful chip, the Ascend 950, delivers roughly half the performance of Nvidia's H100. It finds the binding constraint on Huawei's production is limited supply of high-bandwidth memory: using only Chinese-made HBM, Huawei's output could stay around 1% of Nvidia's through 2028, and even smuggling ten times its entire domestic HBM supply in 2028 would lift it to only about 16%. Does that change your rating?
Makes sense. What is your final number?
